title: Against what does STEGO check the compiler build that a record names, now that the record is the state file?
description: ST-GEN-UC02-R02 says that when the record names a compiler or registry digest that the service's own state does not hold, STEGO reports the record as broken. Since the decision of 2026-10-27 the record is the state file, so the only other state in that file is the input manifest. ST-GEN-INV02 makes the input manifest name the same declaration digest and registry reference as the record, and the input manifest holds no compiler build and no registry content digest. Thus the registry clause has a test (a registry reference that differs from the input manifest's), and the compiler clause has nothing to compare with. Option (a): the compiler clause asks for no check of its own: the record is the only place that names the compiler build, and ST-GEN-UC02-R02 is changed to name the registry reference only. Option (b): the input manifest also holds the compiler build (and the registry content digest), ST-GEN-INV02 and the record format of ST-GEN-UC01-R04 are changed, and a record whose two compiler builds differ is broken. Option (c): the record's compiler build is checked against the compiler that runs drift; this makes every service broken after a compiler upgrade, so it is listed only to rule it out. Recommendation: (a), because a second copy of the compiler build in the same file adds no evidence. ST-GEN-UC02-R02-T02 waits on the answer.

title: Does a promoted component keep its exact digest when it changes to stage alpha?
description: ST-SUP-UC06-R01 says that promotion MUST copy the component into the common registry at its exact digest. ST-SUP-UC06-R02 says that the promoted component MUST enter at stage alpha, whatever its stage was in the local registry. The stage is in the component's own file, so a beta or ga component copied at alpha has other bytes. Reading (a): the component digest leaves out the stage and the sunset, so the copy keeps the digest and only those fields change. Reading (b): the digest covers the whole folder, so a component can be promoted only at alpha, and a beta or ga local component is refused or first moved down. The tests ST-SUP-UC06-R01-T01 and R02-T01 do not assert the digest. Recommendation: (a), and state in a record which fields the component digest leaves out.

title: Where is the reason for an opt-out of a default concern recorded: in the registry or with the service?
description: ST-SUP-INV15 says that the registry MUST record the reason when a declaration opts out of a default concern. ST-SUP-UC10-R02 says that STEGO MUST record the reason with the service. ST-SUP-A1-SR01 says that a run MUST NOT write to the registry sources. Reading (a): the reason is kept with the service (in its declaration and its generation record), and INV15's "the registry" means STEGO. Reading (b): the registry keeps a list of opt-outs, which a run then writes, against ST-SUP-A1-SR01. The tests ST-SUP-INV15-T and ST-SUP-UC10-R02-T01 do not assert the registry clause. Recommendation: (a), and change ST-SUP-INV15 to say that the reason is recorded with the service.

title: Does STEGO refuse a ga component that is below the quality bar, or only report it?
description: ST-SUP-INV07 says that a component MUST be ga only while it holds the quality bar at its current digest. ST-SUP-QRY05 and the step ST-SUP-UC05-FL-S04 show the quality standing of each ga component, so that a component that no longer meets the bar is seen at once; this means that a ga component below the bar can exist in the registry. Reading (a): loading or composing the registry refuses a ga component that is below the bar, so no service builds from it until the evidence is recorded again. Reading (b): the component stays ga and loads, and the quality standing (stego registry quality) reports it and exits non-zero. The test ST-SUP-INV07-T asserts only the report and the refused release, which both readings share. Recommendation: (b), because a new digest of a ga component is made by a release, and ST-SUP-INV07 already refuses that release as ga without the bar; a change to evidence alone then only needs the report.

title: Which tests are a port's correctness tests, which its conformance suite must include?
description: ST-SUP-INV18 says that a port's conformance suite MUST include the port's correctness tests. No record names the correctness tests of a port: the port (ST-SUP-EN06) has a meaning, its field meanings and the path of its conformance suite, and nothing else. As written, the first clause cannot fail. Reading (a): a port lists its correctness tests by name (a new field of the port), and the registry refuses a port whose suite lacks one of them. Reading (b): each field meaning of the port is one correctness test, and the suite must hold one test for each field, named by the field. The test ST-SUP-INV18-T proves only the second clause, the new-enemy test of authz-decision. Recommendation: (a), because a correctness property such as new-enemy is about the port as a whole, not about one field.

title: How does STEGO know that each thing the emitted code must do is stated as its own contract?
description: ST-SUP-UC01-R04 says that each thing the emitted code must always do MUST be stated as its own contract. The test ST-SUP-UC01-R04-T01 can prove that each contract names its code and its test. It cannot prove that the list of contracts is complete, or that one contract states only one thing, because no record says what the things are. Reading (a): this is a review duty of the platform engineer, proved by a manual review at release, with the reference comparison (ST-SUP-SP07) as the check of completeness. Reading (b): it is a mechanical rule, for example one MUST per contract statement, which a check can count. Recommendation: (a) for completeness, and (b) for one thing per contract, written as a rule of the requirement.

title: Does a sample ratio option enable browser telemetry when the page has no deployment setting?
description: ST-SUP-RC03-OC13 says an option MUST NOT enable a signal that the deployment disabled. The emitted runtime.js today enables traces, logs and metrics at the option ratio when the page has no stego-runtime-config meta element, and turns all signals off when the element is malformed. Reading A: no deployment setting disables nothing, so the option may enable all signals (the current code). Reading B: an absent deployment setting is a disabled deployment, so the option must not enable any signal, as for a malformed setting. Recommendation: Reading B, because it fails closed like the malformed case. No test is written for the case with no deployment setting until this is decided.

title: Does a zero tenant fail when the service starts, or when a store method is called?
description: ST-SUP-RC27-OC01 says a zero tenant MUST fail at startup, never act as an empty filter. A store method receives its tenant per call, from a request or a worker iteration, so a zero value appears at call time, not at startup; ST-SUP-RP04-LC01 says every function that takes a Tenant refuses the zero value before any statement. Reading A: the clause means the call is refused before any statement (the runtime rule), and 'at startup' is loose wording. Reading B: the service MUST refuse to start when a configured tenant, such as a worker's tenant list, holds a zero value. Recommendation: Reading A, and change the statement to 'a store call with a zero tenant MUST fail before any statement'; add Reading B as its own clause if it is wanted. No test is written for 'at startup' until this is decided; ST-SUP-RC27-OC01-T02 tests the empty-filter clause.

title: Which declared period does the audit anchor job of the audit-log component run at?
description: ST-SUP-RC28-OC08 says the anchor job runs at the declared period, and ST-SUP-RP05-LC09 says the configured period. The Audit setting (ST-DECL-EN10) has Sink, Retention, Level, Enabled and Reason, but no anchor period. Reading A: the service declaration gets a new Audit setting field, for example Anchor period. Reading B: the period is a fixed setting of the audit-log component's own declaration in the registry, and 'declared' means declared by the component. Recommendation: Reading B, with a fixed default, so the service declaration stays small. The test of the period (ST-SUP-RC28-OC08-T01) names the source once this is decided.

title: Where does a service say audit.pii keep?
description: ST-SUP-RC28-OC01 and ST-SUP-RP05-LC03 let a service keep pii fields with audit.pii keep. The Audit setting (ST-DECL-EN10) has no pii field. Reading A: add a field to the Audit setting, for example PII with the values redact (default) and keep. Reading B: audit.pii keep is a component setting, outside the service declaration. Recommendation: Reading A, so the fleet can list each service that keeps pii in its audit log. The test ST-SUP-RC28-OC01-T02 uses the name audit.pii keep until this is decided.

title: Does a list that returns a pii field write one read audit row per list or one per returned resource?
description: ST-SUP-RC28-OC04 says the emitted code writes an audit row with action read for each list that returns the field. Reading A: one row per list request, with the collection as the resource. Reading B: one row per returned resource, so that the history of one resource shows each read of it. Reading B makes the history query (ST-SUP-RC28-OC09) complete but writes up to a page of rows per list. Recommendation: Reading B, bounded by the page size. No test is written for the list clause until this is decided.

title: May the runtime role read the audit table that the entity history query reads?
description: ST-SUP-RP05-LC10 and ST-SUP-RC28-OC06 give the runtime role INSERT only on the audit table. ST-SUP-RC28-OC09 says that the entity history query reads the local audit_event table, and the service runs as the runtime role. Reading A: INSERT only is exact, and the history query runs through a separate read role or a SECURITY DEFINER function. Reading B: 'INSERT only' means no UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE, and the runtime role also holds SELECT. Recommendation: Reading B, written as 'SELECT and INSERT only', as ST-SUP-RP08-LC09 writes it for the ledger tables.

title: When both the mode option and STEGO_MODE are given, which modes run?
description: ST-SUP-RP09-LC01 says that parsing accepts the mode option more than once and from the STEGO_MODE environment value, but not what happens when both are set, nor how STEGO_MODE names more than one mode. Reading A: the option replaces STEGO_MODE, and STEGO_MODE holds a comma-separated list. Reading B: the modes of both are joined. Recommendation: Reading A, the usual rule that a flag overrides the environment, with a comma-separated list.

title: In which order does a controller release the lease and flush the checkpoint at shutdown?
description: ST-SUP-RP09-LC06 says that, for controller, the sequencer releases the lease and flushes the checkpoint. ST-SUP-RP09-LC03 says that every write under the lease carries the fencing token, so a checkpoint flush after the release has no valid token. Reading A: flush the checkpoint first, under the lease, then release it. Reading B: release first, as the statement lists it, and the checkpoint write is not a write under the lease. Recommendation: Reading A.
